BAGONG PILI-PINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.gov.ph s. 20-4 OPINiON No. 08 KRIZSHELLE ESCOSES CARANDANG 245 Purok 4, Barangay VI-E (Pob) San Pablo City, Laguna Ishelcarandang.ph@gmail com Dear Ms. Carandang This has reference to your email asking for clarification on the proper procedure regarding the appointment of a barangay secretary and clerk. Specifically, you asked: "Gusto kong malaman kung tama ba n a mag-appoint ang nanalong Barangay Chairman ng mga natalong kagawad noong nakaraang election bilang Barangay Secretary ay Clerk. Tatanggalin ang mga nakaupo ngayon sa naturang posisyon at ipapalit and i- appoint na kapartido ng Barangay Chairman. Sana ay mabigyan ako ng kasagutan. " Based on your queries, we came up with the following issues: 1) Whether the Punong Barangay is prohibited from appointing the losing candidates in the October 30, 2023 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections, and 2) Whether the acts of Punong Barangay in removing the incumbents to the positions of Barangay Secretary and Clerk and appointing those who are also members of the party to which the Punong Barangay belongs is proper. As to the first issue, may we invite your attention to Section 94 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 "SECTION 94. Appointment of Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidates Who Lost in an Election. — (a) No elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no elective or appointive local official shall hold any other office or employment in the government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or -controlled corporations or their subsidiaries; (b) Except for losinq candidates in barangay elections, no candidate who lost in any election shall, within one (1) year after such election, be appointed to any office in the government or any government-owned or -controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries." (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the foregoing, as a general rule, candidates who lost in any election cannot be appointed to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries within one year following such election. "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

The rationale behind the one-year prohibition is the extirpation of the "spoils system," considering that the foregoing provision is directed against the so-called "political lameducks" Such general rule however has an exception. The aforequoted provision is clear that if the candidate to be appointed lost in barangay elections, he may still be appointed to "any office in the government" even if the same was made within the one-year prohibition. The case of the appointees subject of your query falls within such exception. Hence, our answer to your first query is in the negative. The Punong Barangay is not prohibited from appointing the losing candidates in the October 30, 2023 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections. As to the second issue, as we understood, the elected Punong Barangay, upon assumption to his office, wanted to replace the Barangay Secretary and Clerk, who we assume were appointees of the previous Punong Barangay. We opine that the action is proper. Please be informed that the terms of office of Barangay Secretary and Clerk are co- terminus with their appointing authority, the Punong Barangay. We have attached herein a copy of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-150 entitled "GUIDELINES ON THE APPOINTMENT OF BARANGAY SECRETARIES, TREASURERS AND APPOINTIVE BARANGAY OFFICIALS," where Section 1 , Article II thereof states that the appointment of barangay secretary and other barangay appointive officials just like the ones subject of your query are, by their nature, co-terminus with their appointing authority. This means that upon the expiration of the term of office of the Punong Barangay who appointed them, the term of office of the barangay secretary and other appointive barangay officials likewise expired. Accordingly, the Punong Barangay may appoint any individual therein, including the previous appointees, taking into account Sections 394 and 395 of the Local Government Code of 1991 on the qualifications required for said positions as well as the concurrence by the sangguniang barangay. This opinion is being rendered based on the representations in your e-mail and without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the court. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, AUTHORITY OF E SECRETARY: AN VICTOR R.
